 By Grace Zokovitch | gzokovitch@bostonherald.com PUBLISHED: November 9, 2026 at 6:54 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... LaMar Cook, a former high-ranking aide to Gov. Maura Healey, pleaded not guilty to charges of SNAP and wire fraud in federal court on Monday.
 Cook, 46, who formerly served as Healey’s Western Mass. deputy director, was arraigned on charges of fraud of benefits over $100 but less than $5,000 and wire fraud, in the Moakley Federal Court in Boston’s Seaport on Monday afternoon.
 The defendant was released on the federal charges Monday but remains locked up on a separate set of charges related to alleged cocaine trafficking out of Hampden Superior Court. Cook was originally released on $25,000 cash bail in March, after police allegedly intercepted 18 pounds of cocaine shipped to his office last October, but had his bail revoked when the additional charges came to light .
 Cook was approved to receive SNAP benefits on April 6 of this year after his initial indictment, the criminal complaint states. The defendant allegedly brought in about $546 a month through the federally-funded program through September, totaling about $3,274 in SNAP purchases.
 On his SNAP application, Cook claimed his “monthly income (was) less than $150” and “money in the bank (was) $100 or less,” the complaint stated, adding they “believe both statements were false.”
 The prosecution cites Cook’s bank account balance of $8,814 in April, and notes that he only lists himself and a child as household member, neglecting to report his fiance and her mother and their additional income. Cook’s mother also won about $1 million from the lottery in early 2026, the complaint continues, allegedly giving her son over $12,000 since March.
 The defendant “omitted substantial household income and assets from his SNAP application,” the complaint alleges, and “purposefully omitted the disclosure” of two employed household members.

 Cook previously defended his SNAP usage to the Herald earlier in the year, stating “I have no income, okay? So, I think anyone who’s facing hardships in the Commonwealth and has no income (should receive benefits).”
 In Hampden Superior Court, Cook is facing additional charges of trafficking in 200 grams or more of cocaine, conspiracy to violate drug laws, possession of a gun without a firearms identification card, possession of ammunition without a firearms identification card, and unlicensed operation of a motor vehicle.
 Cook is scheduled to return to federal court for a initial status conference on Dec. 17 at 11:30 a.m.
